participantInstructions: The event will be presented to you through your reading of the 21st Century Skills, Performance Indicators and Event Situation. You will have up to 10 minutes to make your presentation to the judge (you may have more than one judge). You will be evaluated on how well you demonstrate the 21st Century Skills and meet the performance indicators of this event. Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are a second-year electrical apprentice who earns wages while training. Your contractor lost a large project last month and laid you off, and the unemployment claim you filed now pays $340 a week for up to fourteen weeks. The judge is an investment representative at CEDAR VALLEY CREDIT UNION.

You have $9,000 saved. You need a used work van in about eight months, when your apprenticeship hours resume, and your partner is counting on that van for weekend catering work. Retirement is nineteen years away and you have never invested for it.

A salesperson at MERIDIAN CAPITAL PARTNERS has pressed you to move all $9,000 into the MERIDIAN GROWTH ADVANTAGE FUND, an actively managed fund charging a 4.5% sales load, about $405, plus a 1.15% expense ratio each year. The HARBORLINE TOTAL MARKET INDEX FUND charges 0.04% and no sales load. Your credit union savings account pays 2%.

The representative (judge) has asked you to recommend how to divide the $9,000 between the van and retirement. You could move all $9,000 into the MERIDIAN GROWTH ADVANTAGE FUND, which pays $405 in sales charges and puts the van money in stocks you may have to sell at a loss in eight months.

You could instead keep the van money in the savings account paying 2% and put only the rest into the HARBORLINE TOTAL MARKET INDEX FUND, which gives up growth on most of your savings. The representative (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are an investment representative at CEDAR VALLEY CREDIT UNION. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the apprentice to recommend how the $9,000 should be divided between the work van eight months out and a retirement nineteen years out, and to say which of the two funds, or the savings account, holds each part and why.

During the presentation you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you explain this plan to your partner?
If the van has to wait, what would you tell them?
